subject: design-technology
title: 3D Printing: FDM, SLA, SLS
welcome_lead: Three core additive processes shaping product development.

concepts.def: Building parts by adding material layer-by-layer.
Fused Deposition Modelling — extruded thermoplastic filament.
Selective Laser Sintering — laser-fused powder bed.
Vertical resolution of an additive build (e.g. 0.1 mm).
Sacrificial material holding overhangs during printing.

walkthroughs.body_html: FDM melts a thermoplastic filament (PLA, ABS, PETG) and deposits it through a heated nozzle. Cheap, accessible, but with visible layer lines (~0.1-0.3 mm) and reduced inter-layer strength.
SLA cures liquid photopolymer with a UV laser or LCD. Very high resolution (down to 25 µm), smooth surfaces, but brittle parts and resin handling concerns.
SLS selectively sinters polymer (typically nylon) powder with a CO2 laser. No support structures needed (powder bed self-supports), full mechanical strength, suited to functional end-use parts.
